question: What does this program print, and why?
answer: It prints 8. max starts as the first element, 3. The loop then looks at every later element and, whenever one is bigger than max, max takes its value, so after 8 it never changes. The loop starts at i = 1 because a[0] is already in max, and i < a.length stops at the last index without going past the end. For any array, this code prints its largest element.
